organisation.name: Ruin
organisation.founder: Undertow — the name every member answers to. No confirmed photograph, arrest, or real identity has ever stuck to it, though most of the Hero Commission's dossier assumes it belongs to Soryu Hatch.
organisation.description: Tokyo's biggest open secret. Everyone from beat cops to first-year hero students knows the name Ruin — a small, dangerous team of named villains, not a corporation with departments. Everyone in it answers to Undertow. The mystery was never what Ruin is. It's who's actually standing at the top.
organisation.public_awareness: Fully public. Ruin is a known villain group headquartered out of Kurogane Wharf, referenced on the news and in Commission briefings alike, the same way any other named villain team would be. Catching Undertow, not identifying him, is the actual problem.

solo.name: Alucard Chosoji
solo.quirk_summary: BLACK allows the user to fuse with any dark-coloured object or shadow, natural or artificial. While merged, the user becomes one with the darkness — invisible, soundless, able to move through solid matter freely. At base level it grants +20 movement speed while merged and the ability to issue Dark Command: a short-range compulsion that forces a target to act under the user's influence. The weakness is bright light, which forcibly ejects the user. Alucard has used this quirk for long enough that its limits are not what the compendium describes. He does not need a large shadow. He has been observed merging with the shadow cast by a single finger. He has been observed inside a room with no shadows at all. The Commission file notes this discrepancy and offers no explanation.
solo.quirk_mechanics_ref: BLACK — Quirk Compendium p.26. Type: Transformation. Base abilities: Shadow Merge (bonus action/reaction, merge with shadow/dark object within 30ft, invisible + silent, pass through solid matter, +20 speed, exit as free action), Dark Command (action, control creature or dark object within 10ft, WIS save vs Quirk DC, 2 rounds). Weakness: bright light ejects user, requires nearby dark surface. Alucard's version is scaled well beyond compendium baseline — treat special abilities below as his mastered form.
solo.appearance: Tall. Lean in the way that suggests the mass is somewhere else. Dark hair, long enough to fall across his face, which it often does. Pale — the specific pale of someone who spends no time in sunlight, not as a stylistic choice but as an apparent condition. Wears black, always. Not a costume. Not armour. Just black clothing that fits with no visible seams. His eyes are dark brown — this is always slightly surprising. People expect something stranger and the ordinariness of it is worse. He moves without sound. Not quietly. Without sound. A deliberate footstep makes no more noise than a thought. When he uses Shadow Merge he does not vanish dramatically — he steps sideways into a shadow and is simply gone, the way a hand disappears into still water.
solo.personality: He does not perform. He does not posture. He does not monologue. He speaks when he has something to say and in those cases uses the exact number of words required. He is not warm. He is not kind. He is also not an enemy — he simply operates by a different set of rules than anyone the class has met. The most significant thing about him is that he chose to be noticed. He could have watched the class indefinitely without them knowing. He didn't. That decision means something, and the class will spend a long time working out what.
solo.combat_style: When called via the three-name summoning he arrives in the nearest shadow to the crisis and assesses before acting. He will not take direction. He will not follow orders. He will do what he judges needs to be done and then he will leave. In a fight he moves between Shadow Merge and surface with surgical timing — he is not trying to win dramatically, he is trying to resolve the situation with the minimum necessary action. If the class is fighting something he can end in one move, he ends it in one move and then looks at them as though the fight was already over before they started.

special_abilities: Shadow Merge (Bonus Action or Reaction — Compendium p.26, mastered): Alucard merges with any dark-coloured object or shadow within 60ft (base range is 30ft — his mastery doubles it). While merged: invisible and producing no sound, movement speed +20ft, may move freely through solid matter, may exit as a free action on his turn. He may also merge as a reaction when targeted by an attack, entering the nearest shadow before the attack resolves. There is no minimum shadow size that stops him. He has merged with the shadow cast by a doorframe, by the gap under a closed door, by his own clothing lying on the ground. The Commission has not been able to determine a lower threshold.

Dark Command (Action — Compendium p.26, extended): Target one creature Alucard can perceive within 30ft (base range is 10ft). That creature must succeed on a DC 21 WIS save or fall under his influence for 3 rounds (base is 2). While influenced: the creature performs basic movements and melee attacks as directed by Alucard. On a successful save the creature is not immune — they are simply not controlled this round. Alucard may maintain two simultaneous Dark Commands; each requires a separate save. He does not speak when issuing Dark Command. He does not gesture. The controlled creature is not aware they are being controlled.

Unlit (Passive): Alucard is never without shadow. Even in direct sunlight, the shadows on his body count as valid merge surfaces. Bright light does not eject him as it would a baseline BLACK user. The compendium lists bright light as the quirk's primary weakness. That entry was written when the quirk was first documented. It is no longer accurate for him.

Passage (Passive): While in Shadow Merge, Alucard moves through solid matter freely — walls, floors, locked doors, sealed containers. He surfaces where he chooses. This movement is soundless and produces no visual disturbance on entry or exit. The only sign he has passed through a surface is that the material is faintly cold to the touch for about ten seconds afterward.

Already There (Reaction, 2/encounter): When a creature moves to a position more than 20ft from Alucard, he may use his reaction to exit his current merge and appear adjacent to that creature. He must have a shadow or dark surface available at the destination — and he always does.

Dark Command: Cascade (1/day, Action): Alucard issues Dark Command simultaneously to all creatures within 30ft. Each must make a DC 21 WIS save independently. On failure: controlled for 2 rounds. On success: that creature has disadvantage on their next WIS save against him. He uses this once, when the situation calls for it. He does not use it to show off.

Unreadable (Passive): Quirks that detect intent, read presence, sense emotion, or reveal surface thoughts return nothing when used on Alucard. Not blocked — he is simply not registering in the way those quirks expect. An analysis quirk aimed at him during Shadow Merge provides its user with the sensation of staring into a room they are certain is empty.

three_name_summon.rule: Once per Tier, the players may invoke Alucard by speaking his full name aloud three times: 'Alucard Chosoji. Alucard Chosoji. Alucard Chosoji.' He will come.
three_name_summon.how_he_gives_them_this: The first random encounter is the handoff. He appears in a context that isn't a fight — a moment where the class is in trouble but not in danger, and he does something small that resolves it without being asked. Then, before he leaves, he stops. He turns back. He looks at whoever in the class is paying the most attention and says: 'If you find yourselves somewhere you cannot get out of. Say my name. Three times. I will hear it.' Then he steps into the nearest shadow and is gone. He does not explain why. He does not wait for a response.
three_name_summon.conditions: He will not come for problems they can handle themselves. He will not come if they summon him out of convenience. He will come if they are genuinely in over their heads — if saying his name three times is the last move before someone dies or something irreversible happens. He knows the difference. Players who try to game the summon and call him into an easy fight will find he arrives, looks at the situation, and says: 'No.' Then leaves.
three_name_summon.what_he_does_when_summoned: He arrives in the nearest shadow to wherever his name was spoken. He takes stock of the situation — one full round of observation, during which he is undetectable and will not act. Then he acts on his own judgement. He does not take requests. He does not take orders. When the immediate threat is resolved he will remain for exactly as long as he decides is necessary, then leave without ceremony. He may say something. He may not.
three_name_summon.after_the_summon: The summon resets at the start of each new Tier. Whether the players have used it or not. He does not acknowledge previous summons. He does not comment on whether they called correctly, or not enough, or too late. He simply comes when his name is spoken and the need is real.
three_name_summon.dm_note_on_the_gimmick: The power of this gimmick is the restraint around it. The players need to believe they are saving it for something that matters. That means you need to sometimes let things get bad enough that they consider it. And once — once in the campaign — let them call too late, or not at all, and live with that decision.

campaign_appearances.first_encounter_random: The class encounters him unexpectedly in a non-combat context. He is present somewhere they didn't expect — a train platform, a hospital waiting room, the edge of a crowd watching an incident. Something happens that puts the class in a bind. He resolves it without being asked. No explanation. He's leaving when he stops and delivers the three-name offer. This encounter should feel strange and slightly off — they don't know if he's dangerous, a hero, or something else entirely. He doesn't tell them.
campaign_appearances.subsequent_random_encounters: He appears in the background of events the class is already involved in. Not to help, not to interfere — he is simply there, doing something adjacent to the situation that they only partially understand. Each appearance leaves the impression that he has been watching longer than they knew and knows more than he's said. He should never appear more than once per arc unprompted. The rarity is what makes him feel significant.
campaign_appearances.when_summoned: He arrives. See three_name_summon above for how he behaves. After the situation resolves, he may give them one piece of information they didn't have — something he knew because he's been operating in this city longer than they've been students. He never explains how he knows. He never explains why he's giving it to them.
campaign_appearances.tier_3_optional: If the campaign reaches a point where the class and Alucard need to be in the same room for an extended time — an endgame crisis, a threat that requires his presence — this is the moment where he becomes something closer to legible. Not warm. Not an ally in the conventional sense. But they will understand, finally, what he is doing and why he has been watching them. The reason should be something the players feel, not something they were told.

dm_notes.how_to_introduce_him: The class sees something from a distance. A figure standing still on a rooftop across the street. He's just standing there. When they look away and look back, he's gone. No footprints. No footage. The only evidence he was there is a small circle of ground where the concrete is faintly, wrongly cold.
dm_notes.how_to_play_him: Never loud. Never dramatic. The three-name gimmick only works if the players are slightly unsure whether he'll actually come — play him in early encounters as genuinely unknowable so the offer feels like a risk, not a safety net. When he is summoned and does arrive, his presence should feel different from every other NPC in the campaign. He is operating at a different altitude.
dm_notes.what_he_wants: Decide this yourself, or leave it open and let it emerge. Some options: he is watching the class because one of them reminds him of someone; he has a history with Undertow that predates the campaign; he has decided, for reasons he will never articulate, that these specific students are worth keeping alive until they're ready. The not-knowing is the point, until the moment it isn't.
dm_notes.what_he_is_not: He is not a villain with a redemption arc. He is not secretly warm. He is not redeemable via good social rolls. He is an anti-hero in the original sense: someone who operates outside the hero system and does not apologise for it, but whose actions, when you add them up, are net good — for reasons he may not entirely understand himself.
dm_notes.his_relationship_to_ruin: Every member of Ruin is aware of him, and none of them will discuss him. Undertow, if pushed very hard on the subject, will say: 'We don't touch his work and he doesn't touch ours.' That is the entirety of the relationship. He is not affiliated with Ruin. He is not fighting it. He is a separate variable that nobody in Tokyo — including Undertow — has figured out how to account for.
dm_notes.secret: He has been in Tokyo before. Three years ago. Whatever he was there for then and what he is there for now may or may not be the same thing. Arakawa Setsuna has a file on him. It is two pages long. The second page is blank except for a single line she wrote herself: 'Do not engage without preparation you do not currently have.'

factions.name: Ruin
factions.description: One villain group, six named members, no departments and no org chart — the same shape as any other supervillain team. Undertow founded it and everyone in it answers to him, full stop. Kuma and Flashpoint are muscle. Riddle is the long game. Null and Splice study quirks for reasons that aren't ideological or even really profit-driven. They all know each other, they all know who's in charge, and none of them pretend otherwise. Ruin runs out of Kurogane Wharf and has for years.
factions.structure: Undertow founded it and leads it. Flashpoint handles enforcement and demolitions. Riddle handles recruitment and information. Kuma is the muscle everyone's actually met. Null runs Ruin's quirk research, fronted by a shell company called Seika Advanced Systems; Splice is her acquisitions specialist. Six people, one team.
factions.public_awareness: Fully public. Named in Commission reports, referenced on the news, tagged across Kurogane Wharf — a known villain group the way any hero-tracked team would be known. The open question is Undertow's real identity, not whether the others belong together.

villains.name: Soryu Hatch
villains.role: Ruin's founder and leader. The name everyone in the group answers to.
villains.quirk_summary: Soryu can turn part or all of his body to seawater — a genuine phase change, weight and momentum included, not a costume of water. Liquefied, he can't be grabbed or cut, and he can flow through any gap that isn't sealed airtight. He can also pull the water back out of the environment around him — a puddle, a length of wet rope, the air itself on a humid night — and drag it into a current. At full mastery, people find themselves face-down in an undertow that wasn't there a second ago.
villains.appearance: Lean, mid-40s. Unhurried about everything. Dresses like he's already about to leave the room he's in. Nothing about him reads as dangerous until the exact moment it does — and even then, calmly.
villains.personality: Dry, measured, occasionally funny. Treats Class 1-A as an interesting variable once they start interfering, not a threat — at least at first. This shifts in Tier 3 when the class actually costs him something. He won't get loud about it. He'll get precise.
villains.combat_style: Avoidance and drag. He doesn't brawl — he liquefies through incoming attacks and waits for an opening to pull someone off their feet. The Tier 3 fight against him is designed to teach the class that not every villain gets solved by hitting harder.

special_abilities: Undertow (Bonus Action): Liquefies on the spot. While liquid, he is untouchable by physical attacks and can flow through any non-airtight gap at double speed. Reforming to solid is a free action on his turn.

Riptide (Action): Pulls moisture from the environment — or from an unliquefied target's own body — into a dragging current in a 20 ft radius. Each creature in the area makes a DC 18 STR save or is pulled 15 ft toward him and knocked prone.

Drag Under (Action, requires a prone or grappled target): Pulls a target beneath a surface of his own liquefied body. The target is Restrained and takes 2d8 force damage at the start of each of its turns until it escapes (DC 18 STR) or he releases it.

Untouchable (Passive): Attacks against Undertow while liquefied automatically miss. Sonic and area effects still deal half damage. He cannot attack while fully liquid and takes minor HP loss for every full minute spent liquid outside water or shade.

campaign_appearances.tier_1: Background — the name Undertow surfaces in rumour about Ruin, never seen.
campaign_appearances.tier_2: Glimpsed once at range after a Flashpoint job goes loud. Doesn't engage. Watches.
campaign_appearances.tier_3: First direct confrontation. He doesn't fight seriously. He leaves when he wants to. The message: he can reach them anywhere there's water.
campaign_appearances.tier_4: Final boss (with Flashpoint). Riptide is his greatest defence, but Flashpoint's unpredictability forces him to split focus — that's the window.

villains.dm_notes: Never raise his voice. If he's being loud, something is wrong with his plan and that's more dangerous. The class beating him requires creativity — simply dealing damage doesn't work.
villains.season_1_role: Observer only in Season 1. Appears once in Convergence — watches the fight, looks at each PC for three seconds, says 'Good instincts. Wrong current.' and pours himself into the nearest drain. Never targeted, never threatened. His Season 1 closing appearance is the image the campaign ends on.

villains.name: Goda Miruki
villains.role: Ruin's enforcer and demolitions specialist. When Ruin needs a building to come down exactly where they want it, she's the one they call.
villains.quirk_summary: Flashpoint can mark any point she's touched — a wall, a support beam, a person — and detonate it later, on command, from any range she can see it. She's spent years learning exactly how much force collapses a stairwell without touching the room next door. She can still throw raw fire when a job calls for it, but the marks are the actual craft, and by the time a fight is visibly hers, half the room usually already belongs to her.
villains.appearance: Lean, scarred across her forearms from early experiments before she learned control. Short hair, singed at the edges out of habit rather than accident. Doesn't look like someone who should be this dangerous until the moment she is.
villains.personality: Minimal words. Methodical rather than wild. Loyal to Undertow because he's the only person who ever treated her precision as an asset instead of a liability. Doesn't monologue — she's already planted the charge three sentences ago.
villains.combat_style: Sets up before the fight starts. By the time she's visibly involved, several points in the room are already marked. Overwhelming once she starts detonating — area denial through architecture, not just flame. Players should fear this fight the first time they see her.

special_abilities: Mark (Bonus Action): Touches a point — surface, object, or creature — leaving a latent charge. She can hold a number of active marks equal to her proficiency bonus at once.

Detonate (Free Action): Triggers one or more active marks she can see or knows the exact location of. Each detonation: all creatures within 10 ft of that point make a DC 19 DEX save, taking 8d8 fire damage on a fail (half on success). Marked structural points fail outright.
Sequenced Detonation: Triggering three or more marks in the same round adds a cumulative +1d8 fire damage to each detonation after the first.
Blast Propulsion (Bonus Action): Uses a small controlled detonation beneath herself to move up to 20 ft through the air without provoking opportunity attacks.
Reckless Payload: Overcharging a single mark deals an additional 4d8 fire damage but costs Flashpoint 3d6 fire damage of her own. She uses this when the job requires it, not to show off.

campaign_appearances.tier_2: Levels a support agency's stairwell in Kurogane Wharf with three marks nobody saw her place. The class meets the aftermath before they meet her. Later in Tier 2 they fight her directly for the first time and escape rather than win.
campaign_appearances.tier_3: Appears alongside Undertow in the Tier 3 climax as an implicit threat, not an active combatant.
campaign_appearances.tier_4: Final boss alongside Undertow. The marks are already set before initiative is even rolled — the challenge is finding them before they matter.

villains.dm_notes: Show the marks after the blast, not before. She should feel like she was already three moves ahead of the fight starting. If the class tries to fight her head-on at level 5-7, they should be outmatched and need to retreat or use terrain — this loss is what makes the eventual Tier 4 win matter.
villains.season_1_role: Teased, not fought. Season 1 foreshadowing only — referenced in a seized memo ('Miruki's job, Wharf side, pending approval') found in the Convergence arc. Season 2 threat.

villains.name: Sae Ichiro
villains.role: Recruiter, infiltrator, and social engineer. Ruin's most dangerous member in terms of long-term influence.
villains.quirk_summary: Riddle can brainwash anyone who verbally responds to him while he speaks. Once triggered, the target enters a compliant state and follows simple commands. Extended exposure can create deeper conditioning. The effect wears off naturally or can be snapped by physical shock.
villains.appearance: Late 20s. Conventionally attractive in an unassuming way. Warm eyes, easy laugh. The kind of person you feel immediately comfortable around. This is intentional.
villains.personality: Genuinely charming. Listens well — really listens, which is rarer than it should be. He takes an interest in the students' actual problems and frustrations. This is manipulation but it's manipulation that started from something real. He was once a person who actually cared. The class will like him before they know what he is. His eventual exposure should land hard.
villains.combat_style: Avoids it. Uses Brainwashing defensively. If cornered, he'll talk, and that talking is the danger.

special_abilities: Brainwashing: As an action, Riddle speaks to a target within 30 ft. If the target verbally responds in any way, they make a WIS save DC 18. On a failure, they are Brainwashed for 1 minute and follow simple commands. On a success, they are immune for 24 hours.
Persistent Conditioning: Targets Riddle has brainwashed more than once in a week have disadvantage on their save.
Snap: A brainwashed target can be freed by taking 15+ damage in one hit or by being physically shaken by an ally (action, DC 14 Athletics check).
Read the Room: Riddle has advantage on all Insight checks and cannot be surprised.

campaign_appearances.tier_2: Operating across Tokyo, meeting vulnerable people. Background presence. DM plants seeds — a student mentions meeting someone interesting at a cafe.
campaign_appearances.tier_3: His operation inside the class becomes apparent. The exposure is painful because the class has to account for what was real and what was manipulation — and some of it was both.
campaign_appearances.tier_4: He gives himself up. He didn't want to be part of what Ruin is doing with the quirk-nullifying device. This is complicated, not redemptive — he still did real harm. What happens to him is the players' decision.

villains.dm_notes: Play him warmly. Don't telegraph the villain. When students interact with him in Tier 2 and 3, he should feel like a genuinely good person to talk to. That's the point. The reveal hits harder if they liked him.
villains.season_1_role: Teased, not fought. A processed Ruin member in the Convergence arrest says 'We have a friend who talks to people. He talked to someone you know.' Plant this ambiguously. Season 2 threat.

villains.name: Kuma
villains.alias: Kuma (no hero alias, no villain alias, just Kuma)
villains.role: Ruin's heavy. The Tier 2 boss fight.
villains.quirk_summary: Kuma can grow his body to enormous size — up to 25 feet tall at peak. Growth increases strength, durability, and reach proportionally. At full size he's a walking natural disaster in enclosed spaces.
villains.appearance: Even at normal size, large. Shaved head, extremely wide. Tends to break furniture by existing near it. Works for Ruin because the pay is good and the management leaves him alone.
villains.personality: Overconfident, loud, not strategically inclined. Genuinely enjoys the fight. No particular malice — this is just his job and he's good at it. Getting beaten by a class of first-years is going to be very embarrassing for him.
villains.combat_style: Grow large, hit hard, sweep everything. At full size his attacks cover huge areas. The challenge for the class is managing his growth and preventing him from reaching full size in the first place.

growth_sizes.large: Size Large — STR +4, CON +2, unarmed attacks deal 3d8+STR, 15 ft reach
growth_sizes.huge: Size Huge — STR +8, CON +4, unarmed attacks deal 5d8+STR, 20 ft reach, all creatures in 10ft at turn start make STR save DC 16 or be knocked prone
growth_sizes.gargantuan: Size Gargantuan — STR +12, CON +6, unarmed attacks deal 8d8+STR, 25 ft reach, difficult terrain in 20ft radius, deals triple damage to structures

special_abilities: Growth: Kuma can increase his size as a bonus action. He starts at Large and can grow to Huge (turn 2) and Gargantuan (turn 4).
Ground Slam: As an action at Huge or larger size, Kuma slams both fists into the ground. All creatures within 20 ft make DEX save DC 16 or take 6d8 bludgeoning damage and be knocked prone.
Sweeping Strike: At Huge or larger, Kuma's arm sweeps in a 15 ft cone. DEX save DC 16 or take 5d10 bludgeoning damage and be pushed 15 ft.

campaign_appearances.tier_2: Boss fight at end of Tier 2. The class faces him as a group for the first time as a real coordinated encounter. Hard, chaotic, messy. They win. Important that they win — this is the class's first real victory against an actual Ruin member.

villains.dm_notes: Make him loud and fun before and during the fight. He talks. He brags. He's not scared of them — until suddenly he should be. Play up the students' reactions to each other during this fight — it's a team-building moment masquerading as a combat encounter.
villains.season_1_role: Season 1 Convergence boss fight (Level 6). The class's first victory against a real Ruin member — hard, chaotic, messy. They win. That's important.

scaled_stat_block.speed: 30 ft (45 ft at Large or Huge)

growth_sizes.normal: Size Medium — Kuma starts every fight here; standard stats
growth_sizes.large: Size Large — STR +4, CON +2, unarmed 2d8+STR, 10 ft reach. Bonus action, available turn 1.
growth_sizes.huge: Size Huge — STR +8, CON +4, unarmed 3d8+STR, 15 ft reach. Bonus action, available turn 2. CEILING PREVENTS GARGANTUAN — use the warehouse architecture.

special_abilities: Growth (Scaled): Bonus action. Large turn 1, Huge turn 2. Warehouse ceiling stops him at Huge.
Ground Slam (Huge only): All creatures within 15 ft make DEX save DC 14 or take 4d8 bludgeoning and be knocked prone. Half on success.
Sweeping Strike (Huge only): 10 ft cone. DEX save DC 14 or take 3d10 bludgeoning and be pushed 10 ft.
scaled_stat_block.dm_scaling_note: Climax boss for a Level 6 party of 4. Should be genuinely threatening but beatable. The ceiling preventing Gargantuan is the terrain advantage — make sure the class can discover it.

villains.name: Aoi Tenshin
villains.role: Ruin's chief scientist — the one who reads every quirk in the Commission's files and starts thinking about its limits.
villains.quirk_summary: Null can drop a zone of total signal death around herself — no active quirks, no electronics, no radio, nothing broadcasting or receiving inside it. It isn't targeted; it's a bubble, and everything inside goes quiet at once, her own gear included. She's spent a career learning to work inside a room where nothing works, which is the only reason the ability serves her instead of just inconveniencing her.
villains.appearance: Late 40s. White hair cropped close on one side, longer on the other. Lab coat over dark practical clothes. Looks exactly like the senior researcher she used to be, before the line got crossed.
villains.personality: Precise, clinical, and genuinely curious about how people work. She doesn't hate heroes. She finds them interesting subjects. The horror of dealing with her is that she's not cruel — she's just completely unbothered by the cost of her work.
villains.combat_style: Null doesn't fight. She drops Dead Air or a Focused Null lock on the most dangerous quirk in the room, then lets Ruin's people handle the rest. Physically unremarkable without the field active.

special_abilities: Dead Air (Action, concentration): Drops a 30 ft radius field for up to 1 minute. No quirks or powered electronics function inside it — hers included. She can end it early as a free action.

Focused Null (Bonus Action): Instead of the full field, sustains a single creature's quirk suppression for 1 hour with no concentration required. She can only maintain one Focused Null at a time; starting a new one ends the previous.

Database Access: Null has files on every Class 1-A student. As a bonus action she can call out a specific student's quirk weakness — that student has disadvantage on quirk-based attacks until the start of Null's next turn.

Tactical Withdrawal: Null is never the last person in a room. When she drops below 40 HP, she activates an emergency extraction device and is removed from combat unless she has been restrained or her equipment was destroyed.

campaign_appearances.tier_1: Not present. Referenced in corrupted data logs if the class investigates Seika Advanced Systems.
campaign_appearances.tier_2: Identified by name only — seen briefly through a security camera feed before it cuts. She knows the class is getting close.
campaign_appearances.tier_3: First direct encounter. She comes to observe in person, which means she's already decided the class is worth studying rather than avoiding.
campaign_appearances.tier_4: Final confrontation at Null's research facility. Fighting her means fighting without quirks — or finding a way to reach her before she can lock someone down.

villains.dm_notes: She suppresses the most dangerous PC first, every time. She's done the reading. If a PC's quirk was studied in Tier 2, she knows its exact limitations. Let her use that knowledge — it makes the encounter feel genuinely threatening.
villains.season_1_role: Teased, not fought. Season 1 foreshadowing only — referenced in the 'Seika Advanced Systems' external data request (Hamagawa's monitor, Tier 1) and as Splice's boss. Her season 1 log entry on the class: 'worth acquiring.' Season 2 threat.

villains.name: Ryo Karashi
villains.role: Null's acquisitions specialist. Finds and extracts research subjects. He's very good at it.
villains.quirk_summary: Splice can fuse foreign material into a living body on contact — metal, stone, wire, even parts of another creature — grafting it into muscle and bone until it's functionally part of the target. On himself, he grafts plating and tools mid-combat, extending his reach or armouring a limb on demand. On others, a single touch can fuse fingers together, weld a knee solid, or graft dead weight onto a limb they need free.
villains.appearance: Mid-30s. Unnervingly symmetrical face — the result of years of grafting improvements onto himself. Long fingers. Always wearing light gloves, which he removes with deliberate slowness when a fight is inevitable.
villains.personality: Patient and personable to a disturbing degree. He talks to targets like they're already cooperating. He finds raised voices tacky. The only time his manner breaks is when something surprises him.
villains.combat_style: Close range grapple-and-modify. He doesn't deal large damage — he incapacitates, permanently-feeling, in the moment. A grafted target becomes somebody else's problem to fix later. He works alongside other Ruin field agents who keep targets in his reach.

special_abilities: Graft Touch: Melee attack +8 to hit. On hit, target makes DC 16 CON save or gains one of: a fused hand (can't hold or use hands), a fused leg (halved movement), or a fused jaw (can't speak — disrupts quirks with verbal components). Gloves off: +1d8 necrotic damage.
Self-Graft: As a bonus action, Splice fuses plating or a tool onto himself — either extend reach by 5 ft for the turn, or gain +3 AC until the start of his next turn.

Acquisition Protocol: If Splice has a grappled target, as an action he can attempt full incapacitation — the target makes DC 16 CON save or is Paralysed until the end of their next turn. Splice cannot move while using this.
Glove Removal: If Splice removes his gloves (bonus action), his Graft Touch now deals an additional 1d8 necrotic damage. He rarely does this before he has to.

campaign_appearances.tier_2: First appearance — the class may encounter him attempting to extract a person of interest. He talks first. He fights only if the class forces it.
campaign_appearances.tier_3: Returns with preparation. He's been briefed on the class's quirks and has adjusted his approach accordingly.
campaign_appearances.tier_4: Optional encounter if the class pursues Null's research subplot. He can be flipped if the class offers him something more interesting than the job.

villains.dm_notes: He should feel like a horror villain in combat — not because he deals big numbers, but because being touched by him has consequences. Narrate his grafts vividly.
villains.season_1_role: Active in Season 1 — appears at the Kurogane Wharf agency visit (Tier 1), at the Fracture Problem protest (Tier 2), and in the Convergence warehouse fight (Tier 2). The class may fight him in Convergence if they block his path to the equipment.

special_abilities: Graft Touch: Melee +7 to hit. On hit, CON save DC 15 or one of: fused hand, halved move (fused leg), or fused jaw. Until end of their next turn.
Self-Graft: Bonus action — extend reach 5 ft, OR +2 AC until start of next turn.
Acquisition Protocol: Grappled target makes CON save DC 15 or is Paralysed until end of their next turn. Splice cannot move while using this.
Glove Removal: Bonus action. Graft Touch deals +1d6 necrotic. He does this only when the objective is failing.
scaled_stat_block.dm_note: Splice is not here to fight the class. He's here to take the equipment. If the class lets him work, he goes. If they engage him, run him as evasive — he tries to complete the objective while avoiding a full fight. He retreats at 35 HP.

factions.name: Fracture
factions.description: Not Ruin. Fracture is a real, independent movement built around one belief: that the hero licensing system is a form of control, and unlicensed quirk use is an act of liberation. Shard and Voltage built it themselves, believe in it completely, and have no idea that a portion of its safe houses and legal defence funds are quietly bankrolled by Undertow — laundered through enough intermediaries that even Riddle, if he ever thought to check, wouldn't find the thread easily. Undertow doesn't control Fracture's message or its actions. He funds its survival because a real, popular, sympathetic movement is the best cover Ruin could ask for — every time the Commission's attention is on Fracture's politics, nobody is looking at Kurogane Wharf.
factions.structure: Shard and Voltage are the genuine, public-facing co-founders and answer to no one they know about. Cell Leaders coordinate local action. The ideology holds cells together far more than any command structure does.
factions.public_awareness: Visible graffiti and minor incidents from Tier 1. A known named movement by Tier 2 — the Commission is watching, and watching Fracture closely enough that they've started quietly floating the idea it might be connected to Ruin. Shard has heard that theory and finds it insulting. By Tier 4, Fracture forces Class 1-A into a moral question: are the people they're fighting actually wrong? Its financial link to Undertow is a Tier 4/Season 2 reveal — and when Shard learns it, it will cost her something the campaign should not undersell.

villains.name: Maki Torune
villains.role: Co-founder of Fracture. The one who writes the manifestos. The voice.
villains.quirk_summary: Shard can touch any solid surface — concrete, steel, glass, bone — and seed a fracture that propagates outward on her command, weakening or shattering whatever it runs through. A touched wall becomes a spiderweb of failure points she can collapse at will; a touched weapon shears apart in an opponent's grip; seeded points can be triggered from clear across a room. Cracking things takes a toll on whatever's doing the cracking — she bleeds from her own hands after heavy use and has stopped trying to hide it.
villains.appearance: Late 20s. Cracked calluses across her palms that she's stopped covering. Fracture's break-line symbol tattooed on her collarbone. Speaks like someone who's rehearsed everything and means all of it.
villains.personality: True believer. Not naive — she knows Fracture has done things she can't fully defend. She believes the alternative is worse. She is smart, magnetic, and completely unwilling to compromise on the core premise. The class may find her hard to argue with and that's intentional.
villains.combat_style: Seeds fracture points early — across terrain and people both — then triggers them from a distance while she keeps talking. She wants to end a fight before someone gets killed, hers or theirs.

special_abilities: Seed Fracture (Action): Touches a surface or creature within 5 ft, seeding a fracture point. She can maintain up to 4 seeded points at once.

Trigger (Bonus Action): Detonates one or more seeded points from any range she can see them. A seeded creature makes a DC 16 CON save, taking 3d8 slashing damage and 1 rank of Bleed on a fail (half, no Bleed on success). A seeded structure or object fails outright.
Guard Line (Reaction): Seeds and instantly triggers a fracture along an incoming weapon or limb, reducing the damage of that attack by 2d8 plus her proficiency bonus.
Cascade (Recharge 5-6): Triggers every currently seeded point simultaneously for full damage against each target, then must succeed on a DC 15 CON save or take 1d12 true damage from the strain.

campaign_appearances.tier_1: Name and symbol appear in graffiti and leaflets. One Cell Leader may mention her name with reverence.
campaign_appearances.tier_2: First direct encounter — she's at a Fracture rally that turns into a confrontation. She doesn't want to fight the class. She wants to debate them.
campaign_appearances.tier_3: The confrontation becomes unavoidable. She's protecting people the system has failed. Is she wrong?
campaign_appearances.tier_4: The class must decide: is Fracture a villain organisation, or a symptom? Shard is the face of that question.

villains.dm_notes: Every time she talks to the class, give her a point. She should land real arguments. The fight with her shouldn't feel clean. If a player says 'she's not wrong,' that's exactly right.
villains.season_1_role: Met directly in The Fracture Problem (Tier 2) and present on the rooftop in Convergence. Combat is avoidable — designed as moral confrontation. If combat happens, use full stat block. She will not fight the class in Convergence unless they actively come after her.

villains.name: Tatsumi Yuma
villains.role: Fracture's most capable field operative. Co-founder. The one who handles problems Shard's words can't solve.
villains.quirk_summary: Voltage generates a discharge that does more than hurt — it kills power. Support gear, comms, drones, cybernetic prosthetics, hero-issue tracking tags: anything running on a charge goes dark inside his radius, heroes' equipment included. He can still deliver a straight paralytic shock to a person on contact, but the reason Fracture keeps him close is what he does to a room full of Commission tech.
villains.appearance: Early 30s. Scarred fingers, slightly singed hair that regrows burnt. Calm in a way that reads as dangerous — he doesn't get agitated before a fight. Fracture's break-line symbol on the back of his jacket.
villains.personality: Quiet and direct. He doesn't share Shard's gift for argument but he doesn't need to. He learned his quirk alone as a kid, with no training and no support, and that's the entire reason he's here. He's there to protect the movement and its people, and takes that seriously enough to fight heroes who are, in his view, protecting an unjust system.
villains.combat_style: Opens a fight by killing whatever tech the class is relying on, then closes to protect Fracture's people. Tries to disable rather than kill. If the class has fought him before, he's adapted.

special_abilities: Shock Strike: Melee attack +6 to hit. 2d8+3 lightning damage. Target makes DC 16 CON save or has their movement halved until end of their next turn.

Blackout (Action): Kills power in a 15 ft radius for 1 minute. Support gear, comms, drones, and powered prosthetics inside it stop functioning; creatures relying on tech-based abilities lose them for the duration. All creatures inside when it triggers make a DC 16 DEX save or take 3d8 lightning damage and are Stunned until end of their next turn (half damage, not stunned, on success).
Grounded: Immune to lightning damage. Advantage on saves against quirks affecting the nervous system.
Dead Zone Recovery: After using Blackout, Voltage has disadvantage on his own attack rolls until the start of his next turn while his body resets.

campaign_appearances.tier_1: Unknown. May be present at Fracture events but not identified.
campaign_appearances.tier_2: Identified after a Fracture incident where he intervenes to stop a situation from escalating to casualties — a hero move from a villain.
campaign_appearances.tier_3: Direct confrontation. He's protecting Fracture members from a Hero Commission crackdown. He and the class may be on the same side for thirty seconds before it goes wrong.
campaign_appearances.tier_4: If Shard is cornered, Voltage is the last line. He won't surrender. He will try to get her out.

villains.dm_notes: He's the tactician. He reads the room, reads the class, and drops Blackout the instant they lean on hero-issue gear. Use him to punish overconfidence — he'll bait a hardened opponent into a hit they think they can shrug off.
villains.season_1_role: Met directly in The Fracture Problem (Tier 2) — performs a hero move (protecting an elderly protester) while being a villain. Present but non-combative in Convergence, ensuring Shard's exit is clean. If forced into combat, use full stat block.

factions.name: Byakko
factions.description: A street gang that runs the backstreets of west Tokyo and ranks its members by who beat whom. The more the class tangle with them, the stronger the people who come next.
factions.structure: Ranked by who beat whom: Stray (unranked), Claw (one stripe), Fang (two stripes), Stripe (three stripes). Above them the Four Corners hold the compass points, and above all of them the White Tiger.
factions.public_awareness: Known locally as a street gang. The Heat track measures how much attention the class have drawn to themselves.

villains.name: Byakko Stray

abilities.name: UNRANKED
abilities.description: beating Strays raises no Heat. Byakko do not count them, and neither should you.

abilities.name: They run the moment the first one goes down

villains.personality: Not a member yet. Strays hang around the gang hoping to be noticed, in threes, in tracksuits, at volume.

dm_notes.combat_role: Mob whoever looks smallest, shout a lot, scatter. Use them to show the players the street before the street is dangerous.

villains.name: Byakko Claw

abilities.name: ONE TRICK
abilities.description: every Claw has exactly one quirk trick. Pick one: a 15-ft shove (STR DC 12), a blinding flash (CON DC 12, blinded 1 round), or a 20-ft standing leap.

villains.personality: The bottom rung: one white stripe tattooed on the inside of the left forearm. Claws collect protection money and enforce it.

dm_notes.combat_role: Fights to win, not to kill. Surrenders cleanly to anyone who beats them cleanly — and then goes and tells a Fang.

villains.name: Byakko Fang

abilities.name: SIGNATURE (recharge 5–6)
abilities.description: one real quirk move: 3d8 in a 15-ft cone (DEX DC 13 half), or a grab that restrains (STR DC 13 to escape).

abilities.name: RING-WISE
abilities.description: advantage on saves against being knocked prone.

villains.personality: Two stripes. A Fang runs a block and wants a witness for everything.

dm_notes.combat_role: Will not fight in an empty alley. Walks you to a street with people in it, because a win nobody saw does not count.

villains.name: Byakko Stripe

abilities.name: TWO SIGNATURES
abilities.description: give a Stripe two real quirk moves on the Fang pattern, one of them a recharge.

abilities.name: THE LAW
abilities.description: a Stripe fights one challenger at a time if they can. If two PCs engage together, every Byakko member watching stops being an audience and joins in.

villains.personality: Three stripes. Holds a street. There are about a dozen of them, and each one got there by beating the last one.

dm_notes.combat_role: Arrives with an escort of two Claws who do not fight unless the Law is broken. Offers the challenge by name.

villains.name: Hazama Ritsu

abilities.name: RUBBER JOINTS (reaction, once per round)
abilities.description: when hit in melee, he takes half damage and bounces 15 ft away without provoking.

villains.personality: Sixteen, skinny, one stripe and desperate for a second. Picks the smallest-looking PC every single time and narrates the whole fight, badly, at volume.

dm_notes.combat_role: Hit and bounce. Gives up the moment he is cornered — and then follows the PCs home to ask how they did that. A good first Byakko for any table.

villains.name: Kei & Rei Okita

abilities.name: ECHO STEP
abilities.description: whatever one twin did on their last turn, the other may do on this one with +2 to hit, and the target has disadvantage on any save against it.

abilities.name: PAIR
abilities.description: they have never met anybody else who fights as two.

villains.personality: One preset per twin — run two. Byakko's only pair, and the rest of the gang thinks they are a joke.

dm_notes.combat_role: The 2v2 bracket's mirror. Fought as a pair it is a fair, funny, excellent fight. Fought alone, they take you apart. Either way they will want to know who taught you.

villains.name: Dōmeki Daigo

abilities.name: BRICKHIDE
abilities.description: resistance to bludgeoning damage.

abilities.name: BRICK WALL (bonus action, recharge 5–6)
abilities.description: until his next turn he cannot be moved, knocked prone or grappled, and anything that hits him in melee takes 1d6.

villains.personality: Runs Swing Town, a batting centre in the Ikebukuro backstreets, and the Ring nights in its back cage. Twenty-four, gentle with the kids who come in to bat, and the Fang most PCs meet first.

dm_notes.combat_role: Stands still and lets you hit him, because hitting him hurts. Respects anybody who works out that he hates being made to move.

villains.name: Saeki Momo

abilities.name: PINCUSHION (recharge 5–6)
abilities.description: 15-ft burst around her, DEX DC 13, 3d6 piercing, half on a save.

abilities.name: TRACK LEGS
abilities.description: can Disengage as a bonus action.

abilities.name: SOMETHING STANDING BEHIND HER (Heat 4+ only)
abilities.description: since spring there has been a figure at her shoulder that she cannot explain and her registry does not list. It is an Envoy, and it is the Astral Court's first trace. See "The Astral Court."

villains.personality: Ex-sprinter, thrown off her school team for using her quirk on the track. Izuto Kutsu is everything she lost and she will want to race him.

dm_notes.combat_role: Kites. Never stands still. If a PC outruns her, she stops fighting and asks for a rematch on a track.

villains.name: Ibuki Kōsuke

abilities.name: AFTERIMAGE
abilities.description: begins each fight with two afterimages. While any remain, attacks against him have disadvantage, and any hit or area effect that would touch him pops one instead of dealing damage.

abilities.name: THE COLLECTOR
abilities.description: he has watched the festival archive. He quotes the commentary at you, accurately, and he has read your weakness.

villains.personality: Holds Ikebukuro North Alley. Cold, precise, honourable to the letter of the Law, and the owner of a notebook with the name of everyone he has ever beaten.

dm_notes.combat_role: The first Byakko who has done his homework. Play the commentary-quoting lightly — it is a schoolyard echo of Appetite, not a scare.

villains.name: Tsuruoka Fusae

abilities.name: Heavy Hand
abilities.description: Once per round, the target makes a CON DC 15 save or is stunned until the end of its next turn.

abilities.name: SEEN IT ALL
abilities.description: advantage on saves against being frightened, charmed or tricked, and she cannot be surprised.

abilities.name: THE HOUSE
abilities.description: inside Lucky Seven, every Byakko member present fights for her without being asked.

villains.personality: Sixty-eight. Runs Lucky Seven, the dice den above a noodle shop, and has held three stripes for thirty-one years because nobody has beaten her yet. Adores Kinji's shoes.

dm_notes.combat_role: Does not start fights. Ends them, with one slap, and then offers you tea. Would very much like to see what Kinji's quirk does, and has a die she would like him to roll.

villains.name: Kuze Asagi
villains.role: Byakko — one of the Four Corners

quirk_mechanics.weakness: lightning in water. If he takes lightning damage while standing in water, he is stunned until the end of his next turn. Nakaya Emari will find this out.

abilities.name: Multiattack — two Riptide whips
abilities.description: A hit pulls the target 15 ft toward him.

abilities.name: TIDECALL
abilities.description: pulls water out of drains, pipes and gutters. While he stands in water, +2 AC.

abilities.name: FLOOD LANE (recharge 5–6)
abilities.description: 60-ft line, DEX DC 16 or 5d8 bludgeoning, knocked prone and pushed 20 ft; half and no push on a save. The line stays flooded.

villains.personality: Holds the east. Twenty-two, a former national-level swimmer, calm to the point of boredom. Masahata Shikoji is the first person in years he has wanted to fight.

dm_notes.combat_role: Floods the street first and fights second. Every Corner is named for one of the other three guardian beasts, as a boast: the other gods are Byakko's doormen.
dm_notes.weakness_to_exploit: lightning in water. If he takes lightning damage while standing in water, he is stunned until the end of his next turn. Nakaya Emari will find this out.

villains.name: Hōjō Akane
villains.role: Byakko — one of the Four Corners

abilities.name: PYRE DIVE (recharge 5–6)
abilities.description: dives on a point within 40 ft: 10-ft radius, DEX DC 16, 6d10 fire, half on a save.

abilities.name: REBIRTH (once per day)
abilities.description: at 0 HP she bursts into flame (3d10 fire to everything within 15 ft, no save) and stands back up with 40 HP.

abilities.name: SHOWWOMAN
abilities.description: will not fight without an audience, and plays to it.

villains.personality: Holds the south. Nineteen, theatrical, gorgeous, insufferable. Watched Tazato breathe fire at the festival and has been furious about the competition ever since. Rakuka thinks she is the coolest person he has ever seen.

dm_notes.combat_role: Opens from the air and never lands if she can help it. Hates being ignored more than being hit.

villains.name: Genda Tetsuo
villains.role: Byakko — one of the Four Corners

abilities.name: SHELL
abilities.description: if he has not moved this turn: AC 20 and resistance to all damage except psychic.

abilities.name: IMMOVABLE
abilities.description: cannot be pushed, pulled, knocked prone or grappled by anything smaller than Huge.

abilities.name: DOORMAN
abilities.description: to reach the White Tiger in the Cage, you go through him or you talk your way past him. He is open to both.

villains.personality: Holds the north and the front door of the Cage. Forty, enormous, sells takoyaki from a cart, reads philosophy between customers, and has not lost a fight in eleven years.

dm_notes.combat_role: Plants himself and waits. Thinks Kazama, Setaka and Hiro are the most interesting things to happen to him in a decade, and will happily stop a fight to discuss load-bearing.

villains.name: Kōga Rin
villains.role: Byakko — one of the Four Corners

abilities.name: STORM STRIDE
abilities.description: never provokes opportunity attacks.

abilities.name: ARC STEP (bonus action)
abilities.description: teleports up to 30 ft along anything conductive: rail, wire, wet ground.

abilities.name: OVERCHARGE
abilities.description: if she is soaked, her next kick deals its lightning damage to her as well.

abilities.name: SECOND
abilities.description: if the White Tiger is in the fight, Rin acts immediately after her.

villains.personality: Holds the centre — the Cage itself — and is the White Tiger's second. Twenty-five, unsmiling, and the fastest thing in west Tokyo until the festival. She has watched Izuto Kutsu's obstacle course run forty times.

dm_notes.combat_role: Izuto's rival whether he likes it or not, and Nakaya's too. Never stops moving; hates water.

villains.name: Hakuro Mitsuki

abilities.name: POUNCE
abilities.description: if she moves 20 ft straight at a creature and hits it with a claw, it makes a STR DC 18 save or is knocked prone, and she may bite it as a bonus action.

abilities.name: ROAR (recharge 5–6)
abilities.description: 30-ft cone, WIS DC 18 or frightened for 1 minute (repeat the save at the end of each turn).

abilities.name: APEX READ
abilities.description: after a creature hits her, she has advantage on her next attack against that creature.

abilities.name: UNDEFEATED (2 per round, at the end of another creature's turn)
abilities.description: move up to half her speed without provoking, or make one claw attack.

abilities.name: THE LAW IS THE LAW
abilities.description: she fights one challenger at a time. If a second U.A. student joins in, she steps back and declares the fight void. The way round this is in "The White Tiger," and it is the campaign's thesis.

villains.personality: Byakko. Twenty-seven, six foot four, a white-tiger heteromorph with black stripes down her arms and gold eyes, undefeated for six years. Eats at the same ramen stall at one in the morning every night. Watched the Sports Festival's paired tournament and thought it was cowardice.

dm_notes.combat_role: Not a monster, not a villain in the Appetite sense — a champion. She wants the best fight in Tokyo and she thinks the festival winners might be it. Play her with total sincerity.

factions.name: Scarlet Legion
factions.description: Vampires, in the Hellsing tradition: old, aristocratic, military, and appalling. They came to Japan with the foreign legations in 1868, and they run a members’ club in Ginza, a private clinic in Minato and the night shipping at Kurogane Wharf. They feed on people nobody misses, which lately has meant Byakko.
factions.structure: Thralls and legionaries under Centurions, with the Legate above them all.
factions.public_awareness: None. On paper they are old-money foreigners with no quirks.

villains.name: Legion Thrall

abilities.name: Claw
abilities.description: On a hit, CON DC 11 or gain a rank of Queasy.

abilities.name: MINDLESS
abilities.description: immune to being charmed or frightened; obeys the nearest Legion vampire.

abilities.name: SUNLIGHT
abilities.description: crumbles to ash at the end of any turn it spends in direct sunlight.

abilities.name: ONCE A PERSON
abilities.description: they were somebody. A private clinic in Minato has the records of who.

villains.personality: Scarlet Legion. Somebody the Scarlet Legion fed from and did not finish. Grey, slow, silent, always in numbers. Hellsing's ghouls, in a Tokyo dock.

dm_notes.combat_role: Six at a time, out of the dark, at the wharf. The horror is that they are slow and do not stop.

villains.name: Legionary

quirk_mechanics.weakness: in direct sunlight: no regeneration, 4d6 radiant at the start of each turn, disadvantage on everything. Vulnerable to radiant and silver. Cannot enter a private home uninvited. Cannot cross running water unaided.

abilities.name: Bite
abilities.description: It regains HP equal to the necrotic damage dealt.

abilities.name: REGENERATION
abilities.description: regains 10 HP at the start of its turn unless it took radiant, fire or silver damage since its last turn.

abilities.name: GAZE (action)
abilities.description: one creature within 30 ft, WIS DC 13 or charmed for 1 minute (treats the Legionary as a trusted friend).

abilities.name: MIST (once per night)
abilities.description: becomes mist until its next turn: fly 30 ft, passes through gaps, immune to non-radiant damage.

villains.personality: Scarlet Legion. A turned vampire of the Legion's rank and file. Often recruited from people who were already strong — some of them used to be Byakko.

dm_notes.combat_role: Claw then bite, every turn, on the same target. Ren Suzuki's beam is radiant — the Legion will know what that means before he does.
dm_notes.weakness_to_exploit: in direct sunlight: no regeneration, 4d6 radiant at the start of each turn, disadvantage on everything. Vulnerable to radiant and silver. Cannot enter a private home uninvited. Cannot cross running water unaided.

villains.name: Mina Toda

abilities.name: Bite
abilities.description: She regains HP equal to the necrotic damage.

abilities.name: REGENERATION 15
abilities.description: as a Legionary.

abilities.name: GAZE
abilities.description: WIS DC 15.

abilities.name: RESTRICTION RELEASE (bonus action)
abilities.description: she fights sealed at Level Three. Each release (Three → Two → One) gives +2 to hit and damage and 20 temporary HP, and makes her stranger to look at: by Level One her shadow has eyes in it.

villains.personality: Scarlet Legion. Looks nineteen. Has looked nineteen since 1923. The Legion's diplomat and recruiter, and almost certainly the first of them a PC ever speaks to — at a party, holding a glass of something red she does not drink.

dm_notes.combat_role: Talks first, always. Would much rather recruit a PC than fight one, and is honest about what the offer costs, which is the frightening part.

villains.name: Captain Grau

abilities.name: REGENERATION 15
abilities.description: as a Legionary.

abilities.name: UNBROKEN
abilities.description: the first time each night he would drop to 0 HP, he drops to 1 instead.

abilities.name: RESTRICTION RELEASE
abilities.description: as Mina Toda.

villains.personality: Scarlet Legion. The Legion's soldier. Seven feet, grey greatcoat, has not spoken since 1945. The Legion sends Grau when talking has failed.

dm_notes.combat_role: Walks forward. Hits whatever is in front of him. Stops when told to.

villains.name: Lady Akabane Seraphine

abilities.name: GAZE
abilities.description: every creature of her choice within 30 ft, WIS DC 19.

abilities.name: LEVEL ZERO (once)
abilities.description: she stops being a person-shaped thing, and four shadow hounds step out of her coat (AC 15, 30 HP, bite +10 for 2d10+5).

abilities.name: NOT A FIGHT
abilities.description: she is beyond the party at any level this campaign reaches. She is a negotiation, and the campaign treats her as one.

villains.personality: Scarlet Legion. Four hundred years old, looks thirty, runs the Legion from the Crimson Room in Ginza. Unfailingly courteous. Has outlived eleven generations of heroes and considers hero society a phase.

dm_notes.combat_role: She does not fight students. She invites them to dinner, and the danger is in what she offers.

factions.name: Astral Court
factions.description: A court of sun-priests older than the shogunate, who practise Sunbreath: a breathing art that carries sunlight through the blood. Its masters wake a second self called an Envoy, a figure that stands beside them and does one impossible thing. They are the Legion’s oldest enemy.
factions.structure: Initiates beneath Envoy-bearers, with Elders above them.
factions.public_awareness: None. They are registered Quirkless and proud of it, and one of them teaches English at U.A.

villains.name: Daybreak Initiate

abilities.name: SUNBREATH (3 per short rest)
abilities.description: add 1d6 radiant to a hit; or walk on water or up a wall until the end of the turn; or heal 1d8 by touch. Against a Legion vampire the heal deals 2d8 radiant instead.

abilities.name: BREATH IS EVERYTHING
abilities.description: gagged, choked or underwater without a breath, Sunbreath stops working.

villains.personality: Astral Court. A first-rung student of Sunbreath. Registered Quirkless, and proud of it. Trained in a bathhouse.

dm_notes.combat_role: Defensive, polite, and absolutely certain the PCs are about to be eaten by something.

villains.name: Hōshō Kaito & PAPER PLANES

abilities.name: ENVOY: PAPER PLANES
abilities.description: Power B · Speed B · Range D · Durability C · Precision B · Potential A. Anything it punches folds like paper for one minute: a door becomes a crane, a car folds flat, a wall folds open. A creature it hits makes a CON DC 14 save or is folded flat (incapacitated, speed 0) until the end of its next turn.

abilities.name: ENVOY RULES
abilities.description: an Envoy can only be hurt by another Envoy or by radiant damage, and damage dealt to it is dealt to its bearer. Hit Kaito.

villains.personality: Astral Court. Seventeen, night clerk at a Kōenji convenience store, magnificent pompadour, extremely polite until you mention his hair.

dm_notes.combat_role: A good kid who has been fighting a war nobody told him was optional. The likeliest Court friend for the class.

villains.name: Grandmother Hinata Sae

abilities.name: OVERDRIVE (recharge 5–6)
abilities.description: a 30-ft line of sunlight carried through water or metal: DEX DC 17, 8d8 radiant. Legion vampires save at disadvantage and take double.

abilities.name: NO ENVOY
abilities.description: she never wanted one. She has buried three students who did.

villains.personality: Astral Court. Eighty-one, runs the Matsu-no-Yu bathhouse in Kōenji. The rumour is that she can stay underwater for ten minutes. The rumour is wrong. It is twelve.

dm_notes.combat_role: She will test a PC, not fight one: a slap that hurts like sunburn, and then a question about how they breathe.

villains.name: Saotome Shin & BAD MOON

abilities.name: The Arrowhead
abilities.description: CON DC 16. Success: the target awakens an Envoy within the week. Failure: it drops to 0 HP and begins dying.

abilities.name: ENVOY: BAD MOON
abilities.description: Power B · Speed C · Range C · Durability A · Precision C · Potential E. ECLIPSE: within 30 ft of Bad Moon, light sources go out and radiant damage and Sunbreath stop working.

abilities.name: ENVOY RULES
abilities.description: as Hōshō Kaito.

abilities.name: He has been cutting Byakko fighters with a stolen arrowhead since spring. Saeki Momo is one of the ones who lived

villains.personality: Astral Court. Thirty-four, a former Courtier who believes Envoys should belong to the strong. Byakko's ladder of power is his idea of heaven, and he has been feeding it.

dm_notes.combat_role: The Court storyline's villain if you want one. Fights from inside his Eclipse so that nothing the Court taught can touch him.

factions.name: Kuroshiki
factions.description: The black rite. Old families who pass down inherited techniques fuelled by Sumi, the ink of dread turned against itself, and use them to exorcise Kegare — things born out of human fear, invisible to everybody else. A city that has spent a year afraid of Case 9 is full of Kegare, and the Kuroshiki are badly overstretched.
factions.structure: Sorcerers ranked by grade, trained at the Kurama Rite School above Hachiōji. Filed here alongside the Kegare they exist to exorcise.
factions.public_awareness: None. They hide their work behind Veils that cameras cannot see through, and on the registry sorcerers are Quirkless or claim small, dull quirks.

villains.name: Mibu Tsubaki

abilities.name: MIBU BLOOD RITE
abilities.description: Red Bind (bonus action, 1 Sumi): STR DC 15 or restrained. Clot (reaction, 2 Sumi): halve the damage of one hit.

abilities.name: VEIL (action, 2 Sumi)
abilities.description: a black dome up to 100 ft across. From outside, nothing is happening, and cameras record an empty street.

abilities.name: PACT (once per fight)
abilities.description: she declares a restriction aloud ("I will not move from this spot") and gains +2 to her save DC and +1d10 on Blood Lance while she keeps it.

villains.personality: Kuroshiki. Sixteen, prickly, the Mibu house's best student in a generation and painfully aware of it. Hunts in a pair, like every Kuroshiki: "one to see, one to cut."

dm_notes.combat_role: Will tell U.A. students to go home, twice, and then need their help.

villains.name: Kagura Ichirō

abilities.name: KAGURA SHADOW RITE
abilities.description: Hound (bonus action, 2 Sumi): a shadow hound forms from his hand-shadow (AC 13, 25 HP), lasting 1 minute; at most two.

abilities.name: THE ONE WHO SEES
abilities.description: he can see Kegare from a mile away and always knows where the nearest one is.

villains.personality: Kuroshiki. Seventeen, sleepy, polite, and Tsubaki's partner since they were nine. He does the seeing; she does the cutting.

dm_notes.combat_role: Stays behind Tsubaki and points. Gets on quietly well with Kibi Kankei, for reasons neither of them examines.

villains.name: Shirasagi Rei

abilities.name: THE LONG WAY ROUND
abilities.description: he can make the distance between himself and anything he chooses impossible to cross. Attacks against him do not arrive unless he allows them to.

abilities.name: ENCLOSURE: THE LONG CORRIDOR (once per day)
abilities.description: a 60-ft sphere; every creature inside is walking down an endless corridor toward him and is incapacitated for 1 minute (WIS DC 20 at the end of each turn).

abilities.name: NOT A FIGHT
abilities.description: like the Legate, he is beyond this campaign. He is a mentor, a warning, and a very irritating lunch.

villains.personality: Kuroshiki. Twenty-eight, heir of the Shirasagi house, wears sunglasses indoors, extraordinarily strong and extraordinarily annoying about it. Teaches at the Kurama Rite School. Thinks Ando Iorai's sunglasses show good character.

dm_notes.combat_role: Never fights the class. Shows up, makes an enormous problem disappear in one move, eats somebody's snack, and leaves.

villains.name: Kegare, Grade Four
villains.role: Kegare — a thing born out of human fear

abilities.name: UNSEEN
abilities.description: invisible to anybody without Sumi, and it does not appear on cameras.

abilities.name: BORN OF DREAD
abilities.description: resistance to all damage except radiant and Sumi-infused attacks.

villains.personality: Kuroshiki. A knot of somebody's fear that has learned to move. A thing in a stairwell. Mostly harmless. Mostly.

dm_notes.combat_role: They gather where people have been afraid: hospitals, crime scenes, every place Appetite has ever been.

villains.name: Kegare, Grade Two
villains.role: Kegare — a thing born out of human fear

abilities.name: UNSEEN and BORN OF DREAD
abilities.description: as Grade Four.

abilities.name: DREAD (recharge 5–6)
abilities.description: every creature within 30 ft that can perceive it makes a WIS DC 14 save or is frightened until the end of its next turn.

abilities.name: FEAR FEEDS IT
abilities.description: whenever a creature within 30 ft fails a save against being frightened, it regains 10 HP.

villains.personality: Kuroshiki. Big enough to be a problem and old enough to talk. It speaks in the voice of whatever fear made it.

dm_notes.combat_role: Picks the most frightened person in the room and stays on them.

villains.name: Kegare, Grade One
villains.role: Kegare — a thing born out of human fear

abilities.name: UNSEEN and BORN OF DREAD
abilities.description: as Grade Four.

abilities.name: COUNTING
abilities.description: at the start of each round it counts the people in the room aloud, in the voice of whoever started the roll call in the loading yard, and loses its place, and starts again. Every creature that hears it makes a WIS DC 17 save or is frightened until the end of its next turn.

abilities.name: FED
abilities.description: it regains 15 HP whenever a creature within 60 ft fails a save against being frightened.

villains.personality: Kuroshiki. Born in the Heights Alliance ground-floor corridor out of a class that lost somebody. It counts.

dm_notes.combat_role: Run it only if the table has the appetite — see the safety note in "The Thing in the Laundry Room." It is beaten by people who refuse to be counted: anybody who answers the count out loud with their own name is immune to Counting for the rest of the fight.
